subject: Integration feasibility + latency acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Ng <oliver@edgeanalytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration feasibility + latency acceptance criteria

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured what you emphasized on the call and translated those into measurable acceptance criteria where appropriate.

Pain points you shared:
- Streaming UX: customers abandon when first-token is slow; your product needs visible partial results within ~150ms.
- Burst concurrency: weekends spike to many concurrent live inference sessions (peaks ~400 active sessions, sustained ~120 QPS).
- Tail latency: p95 spikes during batching windows and when KV cache misses occur.
- Operational surface: you need simple autoscaling knobs and predictable fallbacks to lower-cost model variants.

Current stack (from our notes):
- On-prem inference: Triton-backed GPU cluster behind a Kafka-based event bus.
- Model: Open Llama derivative, currently FP16; team is open to quantized variants for cost.
- Auth/network: SAML SSO; traffic heads through customer NAT to your cluster in our VPC.

Success criteria we propose (please mark any mandatory vs stretch):
1) Mandatory: p95 end-to-end token latency < 200ms for single-turn streaming responses at 150 concurrent sessions (first token <= 150ms).
2) Mandatory: sustained throughput of 120 QPS with <1% error rate; graceful degradation when concurrency doubles.
3) Stretch: maintain p99 < 400ms at burst levels (400 active sessions) using model-variant fallback.
4) Operational: PoC must include a clear MOP for cache warming and a runbook for failover to hosted fallback.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood to provide a minimal config snippet and a recommended batching profile (attached).
- Customer to share a sanitized sample trace and typical prompt length distribution (we can accept obfuscated payloads).
- Schedule a 2-week PoC: week 1 smoke tests + integration; week 2 load profile and acceptance run.
- Draft SOW and proposed technical contacts: Laura for onboarding, Karthik for engineering.

Attachments: redwood-config-snippet.txt (snippet with kernel/batching settings) and a SOW draft placeholder (sow-draft-v1.pdf).

If this matches what you expect, can you confirm which items are mandatory vs stretch and whether the PoC dates of Nov 16–27 work for your team?

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.ai]

From: Oliver Ng <oliver@edgeanalytics.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration feasibility + latency acceptance criteria

Jonas — this is great, thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Confirmation of mandatory vs stretch:
- Mandatory: first-token <= 150ms and p95 < 200ms at 150 concurrent sessions — yes, this is table-stakes for our real-time product.
- Stretch: p99 < 400ms at 400 sessions — valuable but not showstopper.

2) Stack notes: we can provide sanitized traces (we’ll strip user identifiers) and sample prompt distributions; expect that by EOD Wednesday.

3) Security / compliance questions: we need to ensure SAML assertion passthrough is doable (we require attributes in the downstream request) and that data-at-rest in any Redwood-hosted component meets our encryption reqs. Are those supported in Private deployment?

4) Timeline: Nov 16–27 works for a technical PoC; we’d like a short kickoff on Nov 16 to align scope.

5) Contracting: we’ll want a clause about fallbacks and incident credits if p95 SLA is missed during the acceptance window — can your legal draft a SOW with that language?

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Ng
Head of Product, Edge Analytics, Inc.
[oliver@edgeanalytics.ai]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Integration feasibility + latency acceptance criteria — next internal steps

Laura / Karthik — forwarding Oliver’s confirmation. Action items below: 

- Laura: please loop Legal to start a SOW draft that includes an acceptance test and incident credit language for missed p95 during the PoC. Attach the sow-draft-v1.pdf as a starting point (placeholder).
- Karthik: can you prepare an initial testing config for Nov 16 kickoff (include batching profile, cache-warm policy, and a simple model-variant fallback)? I’ve attached the redwood-config-snippet.txt we discussed.
- Both: we need an onboarding checklist for their PKI / SAML passthrough and a short checklist for data residency (they’re US-only but encrypted at rest is required).

Let’s aim to have the SOW first draft and the config ready by Nov 12 so Legal and their team can review before the PoC kickoff.

Thanks — Jonas

Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration feasibility + latency acceptance criteria

Quick note — I’m available for the Nov 16 kickoff and can have the first-pass config ready by Nov 12. A couple of technical flags I want tracked before the PoC kickoff:

- Model variant: I’ll test both FP16 and a 4-bit quantized build; we should agree which is the production fallback if latency improves significantly.
- KV cache warm: request their trace sample ASAP so we can pre-warm during the acceptance run — without warm cache p95 will skew high.
- Telemetry: we’ll need to drop a short tracing header in their requests (we support it via X-Redwood-Trace-ID) to correlate tail latency to GPU scheduling.

I’ll add these to the PoC acceptance checklist and share an annotated config (redwood-config-snippet.txt) by Nov 12.

— Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
